name: Germany
tagline: No tuition, and your subject choice decides everything
ownCitizens: If you hold German citizenship, the parts of this page written for other EU/EEA citizens are not about you, and BAföG is your own system. One rule is yours alone: German citizens who did not take German in the IB must prove German before enrolling. Your IB is still a foreign qualification, so the IB entry rules on this page still apply.
summary: In Germany one written rule, the KMK agreement, decides whether an IB Diploma counts at all, and it turns on which six subjects were taken rather than on how many points were scored. Get the combination right and a public university costs a semester contribution of roughly €70–430, which usually includes a transport ticket, and no tuition. Get it wrong and the options narrow sharply or close. Because the rule governs subject choice, it is decided in the first year of the Diploma and cannot be repaired afterwards.
whyConsider: No tuition at public universities for EU citizens, and for most non-EU students too - the exceptions are Baden-Württemberg and TUM in Munich.
A large higher education system, with real strength across engineering, the sciences and the humanities.
German at B2 opens the whole system rather than the English-taught corner of it, and is reachable from a good IB German B.
watchOuts: Check the KMK subject rule before finalising IB subject choices, not afterwards. It is the only requirement on this site that a student in their final year can do nothing whatsoever about.
Most bachelor programmes are taught in German. The English-taught set exists and is much smaller than Germany’s size suggests.

There is no single national application. Medicine and its neighbours go through hochschulstart.de; everything else goes through uni-assist or the university’s own portal, and deadlines vary by institution.
Medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and pharmacy are Staatsexamen programmes of five to six years with no bachelor exit — you commit at eighteen to the whole thing.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: A full Diploma of at least 24 points, with each of the six required subjects graded at least 4. Exactly one grade of 3 may be compensated by a 5 or better in another subject at the same or a higher level.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Set by the KMK agreement of 10.03.1986 in the version of 15.06.2023. Among the six subjects there must be two languages at level A or B (at least one a continued foreign language at A or B HL), a natural science, Mathematics, and a social science. The sixth may be another of those or one of a listed set. This is a rule about the shape of the Diploma, and it is why German recognition has to be checked in the first year rather than the last.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Present in most large cities and concentrated in engineering, business and the sciences, but a small fraction of a very large system.
language.englishProof: Set per programme. An IB taught in English is commonly accepted; confirm against the programme.
notes: German-taught programmes normally require DSH or TestDaF. A good IB German B is a realistic starting point for reaching that, and the prize is the entire system rather than a corner of it.

feeContext.summary: No tuition at public universities for EU/EEA citizens. A semester contribution of roughly €70–430 is payable, usually including a local or regional transport ticket. Non-EU students pay €1,500 per semester in Baden-Württemberg and usually €2,000–3,000 per semester at TUM (new students since winter 2024/25).

sectorLandscape.summary: Germany splits its institutions by purpose rather than by prestige, and the split is sharper than in most systems. A Universität researches and awards doctorates; a Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften teaches a profession and traditionally does not. Alongside them sit the dual universities, where study alternates with paid work at a company that selects you, and the art and music academies, which admit on audition. Most of this is invisible from outside Germany, where "German university" usually means the first category only.

routes.what: The research universities, including the Technische Universitäten. Academic in emphasis, strong in theory, with a three-year Bachelor followed by a two-year Master that most students treat as part of the same course rather than as optional.

Often abbreviated HAW, and previously Fachhochschule. Professionally focused, with smaller groups, compulsory placements and teaching staff who have worked in the field. Excellent for engineering and business, and far better regarded by German employers than the English translation suggests.
routes.note: Neither a lesser university nor a polytechnic nor a college. The German distinction is about research remit and professional orientation, not about standing.

routes.what: Study alternating with paid work at a partner company, typically in three-month blocks, ending in a Bachelor and usually a job. You apply to the company first and the place follows from that, so the employer is the real selector and the timetable runs a year ahead of ordinary admissions.
routes.note: Almost always taught in German, and almost never mentioned to international students. Worth knowing it exists, because for the right student it is the strongest version of what Germany offers.

routes.what: Fine art, design, music and drama, admitting on portfolio or audition on their own calendars, often earlier than everything else. Grades are close to irrelevant beside the work.

A preparatory year ending in the Feststellungsprüfung, for applicants whose school qualification does not give direct access. A full IB Diploma meeting the KMK subject rule does give direct access, so this is normally not needed — which is exactly why it is worth knowing about if the subject rule is not met.
routes.note: Taught in German. Recorded because it is the route that exists when the KMK rule has not been satisfied.

notes: The KMK agreement is a PDF and cannot be re-read automatically. It needs a person each cycle, and its annexes carry separate revision dates.
hochschulstart dates recorded are the published 2026 ones; 2027 dates are not yet published. Re-check from spring 2027.

Established 2026-09-24: Baden-Württemberg (€1,500 per semester) and TUM (usually €2,000–3,000 per semester for a bachelor's) charge non-EU students. Other states and universities not checked one by one.
